name: date-time-pickers
summary: The product's date/time selection family. The hero is TimeRangePicker (42×) — the observability time-range control (relative presets + absolute custom range). MDatePicker (10×, wraps a-date-picker) is the form date-time field, in practice ALWAYS used with show-time. MTimePicker wraps a-time-picker (12-hour) but is rarely used standalone. DateTimePopover is a lighter custom-range-only popover. TimeRangeSlider is a FUNCTIONAL, LINKABLE timeline scrubber — drive its window/band from a range picker via range-start/range-end.
selectHint: Pick a chart/dashboard/log TIME WINDOW → range (or range-presets); a date/time VALUE in a form → field-datetime/field-date/field-time; a draggable timeline SCRUBBER (optionally linked to a range picker) → slider.

kind.description: which family member to render — range (the 42× hero TimeRangePicker), range-presets (hide-custom, 24×), field-datetime / field-date / field-time (MDatePicker/MTimePicker fields), slider (TimeRangeSlider scrubber)

allowClear.description: attr allow-clear — a times-circle × on the range pill that resets the selection (7×)

empty.description: start with no selection — shows the calendar icon + “Select Time” placeholder

size.description: '' (default 28px) | 'lg' → a 35px-tall range trigger that lines up with the 35px toolbar/action buttons

showRange.description: attr show-range — print the RESOLVED absolute window beside the preset pill (two lines: from → to, e.g. 'Wed, Sep 02 06:04 PM' / 'Thu, Sep 03 06:04 PM'), like the product TimeRangePicker on a dashboard header

rangeStart.description: slider-only — drive the scrubber's window/band from OUTSIDE (epoch ms). Set together with range-end to LINK the slider to a range picker's selection: the band snaps to [range-start, range-end] and the axis window auto-fits AROUND that range (padding = max(50% of the span, 6h)). 0 (default) = unlinked (the slider uses its own today ± 5 days window).

rangeEnd.description: slider-only — the end of the linked window (epoch ms). Must be > range-start for the link to engage; then the band's right handle snaps here and the axis format adapts (DD/MM for a multi-day window, HH:MM for ≤3 days). 0 (default) = unlinked.

variants.name: TimeRangeSlider
variants.what: FUNCTIONAL draggable scrubber — band + two handles, DATE axis, LINKABLE to a range picker via range-start/range-end

sizes.name: default
sizes.note: compact range trigger (size unset) — the default

sizes.name: lg
sizes.note: attr size="lg" — taller range trigger that lines up with the 35px toolbar/action buttons and gives the show-range readout room

TimeRangePicker.renders: REFERENCE REPRODUCTION in Storybook (depends on the Vuex user-preference store + the `datetime` filter + moment, so it can't render live — like the Kendo grid).

props.value: v-model — object { selectedKey, startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime, dailyRollingData }
props.hideCustomTimeRange: bool, 24× — drop the 'Custom' option (presets-only mode); the dominant variant
props.excludedOptions: array, 7× — drop specific preset keys (e.g. ['today']); a real, common variant
props.allowClear: bool, 7× — show a times-circle × to reset (emits change=undefined)
props.maxSelectableRangeDays: number, default 93 (365 for report export) — disables dates beyond the span in the custom calendar (2×)
props.bordered: bool, 1× — add a --border-color frame to the trigger
props.pillStyle: object, 1× — inline style for the shortcut pill
props.hideSelectedTime: bool, 1× — hide the absolute from/to shown beside the trigger
props.onlyLabel: bool — DECLARED BUT UNUSED (0×); dailyRolling also 0×

TimeRangePicker.emit: change/v-model -> { selectedKey:'-24h'|'today'|'custom'|…, startDate:<ms>, endDate:<ms>, startTime:'HH:mm:ss', endTime:'HH:mm:ss', dailyRollingData:false }. Custom range validates end > start or blocks the emit.
TimeRangePicker.trigger: a --timerange-background-color shortcut pill (e.g. '24h' or a computed duration '6d 23h') + separator + the range label ('Last 24 Hours'); empty state shows a calendar-alt icon + 'Select Time'.

props.showTime: bool|object, default { use12Hours:true, format:'hh:mm A' } — ALL 10 real usages pass :show-time, so MDatePicker is the date-TIME field

MDatePicker.icon: calendar suffix icon; slot dateRender for custom day cells

MTimePicker.usage: 0× standalone — NOT used as a standalone tag anywhere in src. Time-of-day is entered via MDatePicker show-time or inside the TimeRangePicker custom view.

TimePicker (custom).usage: 0× standalone; used INSIDE TimeRangePicker's custom view (From/To time)
TimePicker (custom).renders: internal — wraps FlotoDropdownPicker (a DROPDOWN of time options + clock icon), NOT an Ant spinner

TimeRangeSlider.renders: FUNCTIONAL reproduction in the Elements element — a draggable band + two round handles on a tick rail with a DATE axis; the product original is an Ant range Slider (needs moment/helper/datetime filter).
TimeRangeSlider.anatomy: a tick rail (100 dots) inset by --page-header-padding so the timeline aligns with the page header; a draggable BAND (--slider-tracker, 14px tall, 4px border-radius) between two round handles (--page-background-color fill, --neutral-light border). Handles show a hover RING (--page-text-color) and a datetime TOOLTIP (--tooltip-background-color / --active-text-color) above them; the tooltip PERSISTS while dragging (a .dragging class), showing the resolved datetime as the handle moves. DATE axis labels every 10th tick with ADAPTIVE format — DD/MM for a multi-day window, HH:MM for a short (≤3-day) window — and the first/last labels are anchored (translateX 0 / -100%) so they don't overflow the ends.
TimeRangeSlider.window: By default the axis window spans today ± 5 days (10 days). When range-start/range-end are supplied (link mode), the window fits AROUND that range with padding = max(50% of the span, 6h) and the band snaps to [range-start, range-end] — so the slider GROWS/SHRINKS with a linked range picker's selection.
TimeRangeSlider.linkable: Set the range-start/range-end props (epoch ms) to link the slider to a range picker: when that picker's `change` emits fromMs/toMs, feed them into the slider's range-start/range-end and the band + window follow.
TimeRangeSlider.emit: change -> { startPct, endPct, start, end } — startPct/endPct are the handle positions (0–100), start/end the RESOLVED datetimes at those positions (e.g. 'Wed, Sep 02, 2026 06:04:00 PM'). The product original emits { selectedKey:'custom', startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime }.

DateTimePopover.usage: 1× (SLO correction profile) — a lighter CUSTOM-RANGE-ONLY popover (no presets)

decisionFlow: Selecting a TIME WINDOW for charts/dashboards/logs (relative or absolute)? -> TimeRangePicker (the 42× hero).
Want presets only (no absolute calendar)? -> TimeRangePicker :hide-custom-time-range (24×).
A single date or date+time value in a FORM field? -> MDatePicker with :show-time (the product default).
Just a time of day (e.g. a schedule)? -> MTimePicker (12-hour).
A custom absolute from/to with NO presets, as a form field? -> DateTimePopover.
A draggable timeline SCRUBBER over the current window? -> slider (TimeRangeSlider). LINK it to a range picker by feeding that picker's change fromMs/toMs into the slider's range-start/range-end.
Need the trigger to line up with 35px toolbar buttons, or to print the resolved absolute window? -> size='lg' and/or show-range on the range trigger.

presetsOnly.example: widgets where only relative windows make sense

dateTimeField.useWhen: a date+time value in a form

TimeRangePicker.useWhen: Selecting a TIME WINDOW for charts, dashboards, or log/metric explorers — relative presets (Last 5/15/30 Mins, Last 1/6/12/24/48 Hours, Today, Last Day, Last/This Week, Last/This Month) OR an absolute custom from/to range. This is the 42x hero control and the default answer for any observability time selection. Emits v-model { selectedKey, startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime }.
TimeRangePicker.dontUse: Don't use for a single date/date-time value in a form (use MDatePicker with :show-time), for a time-of-day schedule (MTimePicker), or when absolute custom ranges must be forbidden (use presets-only via :hide-custom-time-range). Don't hand-roll a relative-range dropdown — this is that control.
TimeRangePicker.example: The dashboard/metric-explorer/log-search time-window control — click the '24h' pill to open the preset list, or choose Custom for a dual-month absolute range with From/To time selects.

presets-only.useWhen: You need TimeRangePicker but absolute custom ranges shouldn't be allowed — pass :hide-custom-time-range to drop the 'Custom' option and expose only the relative presets. The dominant configured variant (24x). Use for widgets/contexts where only relative windows make sense.
presets-only.dontUse: Don't use when users legitimately need to pick an absolute from/to calendar range — use the full TimeRangePicker (Custom enabled). Don't reach for a separate component; this is just TimeRangePicker with one prop.
presets-only.example: Widgets and panels where only relative rolling windows are valid — the preset list (Last 24 Hours, Last Week, etc.) with no absolute calendar.

excluded-options.useWhen: You want TimeRangePicker but must hide specific preset keys that don't apply to the context — pass :excluded-options with an array of preset keys (e.g. ['today']) to drop just those presets while keeping the rest. A real, common variant (7x).
excluded-options.dontUse: Don't use to remove the Custom range wholesale — that's :hide-custom-time-range (presets-only). Don't use if you need every preset; only reach for it when specific presets are invalid for the view.
excluded-options.example: A view where a preset like 'Today' is meaningless is dropped via :excluded-options="['today']" while the remaining relative windows stay available.

MDatePicker.useWhen: A single date or date+time value in a FORM field. In the product it is ALWAYS used with :show-time (12-hour hh:mm A), so treat it as the date-TIME field with a calendar icon. Constrain with :min-date (7x) or :disabled-date, add :allow-clear for an × (9x).
MDatePicker.dontUse: Don't use for selecting a chart/dashboard time WINDOW — that's TimeRangePicker. Don't use for a bare time-of-day (use MTimePicker) or a presets-free custom range popover (DateTimePopover). Don't pass an empty string '' as the value — moment parses it to 'Invalid date'; pass null/undefined or a moment.
MDatePicker.example: A maintenance-window start or schedule date-time field: <MDatePicker :show-time :min-date :allow-clear v-model> opening a single-month calendar with a 12-hour time spinner.

MTimePicker.useWhen: Just a time of day (e.g. a daily run time / schedule), rendered as a 12-hour picker with a clock icon (allow-clear default true). Documented for reference — wraps a-time-picker.
MTimePicker.dontUse: Don't reach for it as a standalone control in practice: the product uses NO standalone time picker — time-of-day is entered via MDatePicker :show-time or inside the TimeRangePicker custom view (which uses a custom dropdown-based TimePicker). Don't use for a date or date-time value (MDatePicker) or a time window (TimeRangePicker). Don't pass '' as the value (parses to Invalid date).
MTimePicker.example: A daily run-time / schedule time-of-day field (12-hour hh:mm A) — reference pattern; in real product code time-of-day arrives via MDatePicker show-time or the range custom view instead.

TimeRangeSlider.useWhen: You need a draggable TIMELINE SCRUBBER over an existing time window — a tick rail with a DATE axis and two round handles that drag a band to reshape the selected window. It is FUNCTIONAL (kind="slider"): dragging emits change { startPct, endPct, start, end } and the handle tooltip shows the resolved datetime live while dragging. It is LINKABLE — pass range-start/range-end (epoch ms) to fit its window around, and snap its band to, a range picker's current selection (feed that picker's change fromMs/toMs in). The axis format adapts DD/MM ↔ HH:MM to the window length.
TimeRangeSlider.dontUse: Don't use as the primary way to pick a window when users expect presets — pair it with (or LINK it to) TimeRangePicker rather than replacing it. Don't use in forms or for discrete date/time values. Only 2x — a specialized scrubber, not the default. Don't set only one of range-start/range-end (the link needs both, with end > start) or it stays in the default today ± 5-day window.
TimeRangeSlider.example: The dashboard timeline scrubber and the alert-correlation drawer — drag the two handles to reshape the visible window; or link it below a TimeRangePicker so the band tracks the picker's selection.

DateTimePopover.useWhen: A custom absolute from/to range as a FORM field with NO presets — a lighter custom-range-only popover (built on MPopover + FlotoFormItem). Emits { startDate, endDate, startTime, endTime }.
DateTimePopover.dontUse: Don't use when relative presets are wanted (use TimeRangePicker or presets-only) or for a single date-time value (MDatePicker). Rare (1x) — only when you specifically need an absolute from/to inside a form without the preset machinery.
DateTimePopover.example: The SLO correction-profile form — a custom-range-only from/to popover with no relative presets.

change.when: fires on every pick / drag AND on initial mount (the selection is also reflected to el.value as JSON).
change.detailNote: Per Vue custom-element convention the payload is array-wrapped — read CustomEvent.detail[0].

payloadByKind.range / range-presets (relative): { type:'relative', key:'-24h'|'today'|…, label:'Last 24 Hours', span:'24h', fromMs:<ms>, toMs:<ms>, from:'Wed, Sep 02, 2026 06:04:00 PM', to:'Thu, Sep 03, 2026 06:04:00 PM' } — fromMs/toMs/from/to are the RESOLVED absolute window (relative presets resolved against now; period presets like Today/This Week/This Month resolved from the period start).
payloadByKind.range / range-presets (custom absolute): { type:'absolute', start:<ms>, end:<ms>, fromTime:'10:05', toTime:'…', fromMs:<ms>, toMs:<ms>, from:'…', to:'…' }.
payloadByKind.field-date / field-datetime: { date:<ms>, display:'02/09/2026 06:04 PM' } (date-only omits the time).
payloadByKind.slider: { startPct:<0-100>, endPct:<0-100>, start:'Wed, Sep 02, 2026 06:04:00 PM', end:'Thu, Sep 03, 2026 06:04:00 PM' } — start/end are the resolved datetimes at the two handle positions.

change.link: For a range/preset kind, take change.fromMs/toMs and set them as range-start/range-end on a kind='slider' element to keep the slider's window + band in sync with the picker.

do: Use TimeRangePicker for chart/dashboard/log time windows.
Use :hide-custom-time-range when only relative windows are valid.
Use MDatePicker WITH :show-time for date-time form fields (the product norm).
Constrain selection with :max-selectable-range-days / :min-date where it matters.
Use size='lg' to line the range trigger up with 35px toolbar/action buttons, and show-range to print the resolved absolute window beside the pill.
LINK the slider to a range picker: read the picker's change fromMs/toMs and set them as range-start/range-end on the kind='slider' element so its window + band track the selection.
Read the change payload's resolved fromMs/toMs/from/to (range/preset kinds) or start/end (slider) instead of re-deriving the window yourself.
dont: Don't hand-roll a relative-range dropdown — use TimeRangePicker.
Don't use a bare date picker for chart windows — that's TimeRangePicker's job.
Don't pass an empty string '' to MTimePicker/MDatePicker value (parses to an Invalid date) — pass null/undefined or a moment.
Don't assume card/inline calendar variants — the product uses the popup pickers only.
Don't set only one of range-start/range-end on the slider — the link needs BOTH (with end > start) or it stays in the default today ± 5-day window.
Don't read CustomEvent.detail directly — it's array-wrapped; read detail[0].

F1.issue: TimeRangePicker depends on the user-preference store + datetime filter, so it is reproduced (not rendered live) in Storybook.

F2.issue: Catalog-wide focus-ring removal (SF-001) may affect the picker inputs/preset rows; verify keyboard focus visibility.

F3.issue: The slider's horizontal inset uses --page-header-padding (8px fallback) so it aligns with a page header; if the host app doesn't define that var the slider falls back to 8px insets — set --page-header-padding on the container to match your header.

knownIssues.element: [element] The obs-date-time-picker element is FUNCTIONAL (not reference-only): it reflects the current selection to el.value as JSON and emits a `change` event on every pick/drag (payload varies by kind — see events). It has no value SETTER prop, so you can't programmatically pre-set a date; for the slider, drive its window/band via range-start/range-end. For full product parity (store/moment-backed resolution) use the product component in-repo or STOP-and-ASK.

accessibility.providedByAnt: a-date-picker / a-time-picker expose a text input + a keyboard-navigable calendar/time panel; Escape closes; the input is focusable and typeable.
accessibility.verify: Focus-visible ring (SF-001) on inputs and on the TimeRangePicker preset rows (which are <a>/clickable divs — ensure they're keyboard-reachable and labelled).

scopedOut.Scheduler / Recurrence (schedule-input/): 17 files — a Once/Daily/Weekly/Monthly RECURRENCE builder (MRadioGroup + Once/Weekly/Monthly inputs). Date/time-adjacent but a DISTINCT component family — candidate for its own future entry, not part of date/time pickers.
scopedOut.date-remark-pairs.vue: a date + remark list (holidays / special days) — a composite, not a picker primitive.
scopedOut.TimeRangeSlider text-input shorthand (ti: internal — typed shorthand ('5m','7d') with autocomplete inside TimeRangePicker.
scopedOut.kit DateRangePicker / NotifyTimePicker: 0× / niche — not used as standalone product patterns.

a11y.summary: Focusable text input + keyboard-navigable calendar; disabled via the disabled input. The trigger pill should expose its current selection to AT. The slider handles are mouse-drag only in this element — provide a keyboard-operable range control (or the range picker) for keyboard/AT users.
issues: Range error is shown as text.
Slider handles are drag-only (mousedown/mousemove) — no keyboard (arrow-key) operation or ARIA slider role; pair with the range picker for accessible selection.
a11y.$note: Catalogue-wide gap SF-001 = no visible :focus-visible ring; tracked in findings/.

changelog: 2026-09-07 — Made the TimeRangeSlider functional and LINKABLE: new range-start/range-end props drive its window/band (link it to a range picker); dynamic window fits the selection with adaptive DD/MM↔HH:MM axis; band radius 4px; handle tooltip persists while dragging; horizontal inset matches the page header (--page-header-padding) with anchored end labels; range/preset change events now carry resolved fromMs/toMs/from/to. Also added size='lg' and show-range.

2026-07-14: fixed the left double-chevron « (owner) — the calendar header/month/year/decade nav used chevronDoubleRight + inline transform:scaleX(-1), which does NOT reliably flip on the <obs-icon> host (Vue custom-element upgrade interferes), so it rendered » on the LEFT. Added a real `chevronDoubleLeft` icon (mirrored path) and used it directly across all popovers — no transform.

2026-07-14: completeness pass (owner) — added the element 'kinds & when to use' table (range · range-presets · field-datetime · field-date · field-time · slider) + the shared props (disabled/bordered/allow-clear/empty/placeholder) + the decision routing to the prose spec. Playground already switches all 6 kinds; registry already complete.

2026-06-30: added to the Elements site — obs-date-time-picker, the date/time family as one element via a `kind` prop: range (the 42× TimeRangePicker hero — interactive pill → presets → Custom dual-month calendar with From/To time menus), range-presets (hide-custom 24×), field-datetime/field-date/field-time (MDatePicker/MTimePicker fields + disabled), slider (draggable TimeRangeSlider). Reference reproductions with real tokens (--timerange-*, --calendar-selected-day-background-color, --slider-tracker, --dropdown-*); gated by cross-render token check (light+dark) + driven open/custom/disabled states.

2026-06-30: made the MDatePicker/MTimePicker FIELD kinds interactive (owner caught they were static, non-functional) — field-date/field-datetime open a single-month calendar (today ringed, allow-clear ×), field-datetime adds a 12h time field, field-time opens a 12h time menu; reset popups on kind-change. Playground fixes: slider now fills the stage width; tall picker panels no longer clip (stage top-aligns + overflow visible + min-height).

2026-06-30: reworked the MDatePicker/MTimePicker field popovers to match the real Ant render (owner compared to Storybook) — a connected card with the value input on top, the calendar (today navy-filled), a footer (Now · select time/select date · Ok), and a proper 3-COLUMN time spinner (HH · MM · AM/PM, selected row banded + scrolled to top) instead of a flat time dropdown. field-date = Now·Ok, field-time = the spinner alone.

2026-06-30: matched the per-variant footer pattern (owner) — date-only shows a single centered "Today" link (not Now·Ok); time-only keeps Now·Ok; date-time keeps Now·select-time/date·Ok with the time spinner opening in the same popover.

2026-06-30: fixed field-calendar day states (owner) — selected (filled navy) and today (navy RING) were rendering identically; now distinct, plus a hover background on days. Applies to field-date and field-datetime (refactored day cells from inline styles to CSS classes so :hover works).

2026-07-14: FUNCTIONAL now (owner) — obs-date-time-picker reflects the selection to `el.value` (JSON) and emits a `change` event on every pick, so it's no longer reference-only. Value shape varies by kind: range/range-presets → {type:'relative',key,label,span} or {type:'absolute',start,end,fromTime,toTime}; field-date/field-datetime → {date:<ms>,display}; field-time → {time}; slider → {startPct,endPct,start,end}. Verified initial reflection + change on preset/day/time/slider selection.

2026-09-03: dashboard-header + slider fidelity pass (owner, from the ObserveOps DS starter's Alert Summary rebuild), shipped in elements 0.1.168. RANGE trigger: new `size='lg'` (35px trigger to line up with the 35px toolbar/action buttons — the compact default is 28px) + new `show-range` attr that prints the RESOLVED absolute window beside the pill (two lines from → to, computed from the selected preset/custom against now), matching the product TimeRangePicker. SLIDER: band height 18px → 14px, dots 20% smaller (8→6.4px) and vertically centered on the band, a hover state (ring) + a dark datetime tooltip above each handle (--tooltip-background-color / --active-text-color), and .slider-wrap bottom padding 36px → 18px (was leaving a big gap under the timeline labels). Verified render in the starter (light); registry props (size, showRange) updated.
elementValue: reflects el.value (JSON) + emits `change` (array-wrapped detail — read detail[0]). Per-kind: range/range-presets → relative {type,key,label,span,fromMs,toMs,from,to} | absolute {type,start,end,fromTime,toTime,fromMs,toMs,from,to}; field-date/datetime → {date:<ms>,display}; field-time → {time}; slider → {startPct,endPct,start,end}. The slider's window/band are driven from OUTSIDE via range-start/range-end (epoch ms) to link it to a range picker.
